action: Seekom advises guests not to click links, pay or share card details in response to unexpected messages, and to contact the provider using official details.
date_note: Seekom's notice says it identified unauthorised access on 20 November 2026.
exec: Seekom says guest booking data may have been accessed, and its accommodation customers are advised to warn guests.
geo_basis: operator region (Kaipara District, Northland) as stated by the article
plain: Seekom, a booking system used by accommodation providers, says an unknown party accessed its platform. Some guests have had suspicious WhatsApp messages; Seekom says they appear to contain booking information but it cannot know for sure.

sources.name: Seekom, Cyber Security Incident Update (page updated 25 Nov 2026)

summary: Seekom says it identified unauthorised access to iBex, its online booking and property management platform, on 20 November 2026. It says, preliminarily, that names, contact details, dates of birth and masked payment details may have been accessed. It says reports of suspicious WhatsApp messages appear to contain booking information from its platform, though it cannot know for sure. Kai Iwi Lakes Campground told the NZ Herald the messages did not come from it.
title: Seekom confirms unauthorised access to its iBex booking platform; Northland campgrounds warn customers

validation.note: Seekom's own notice (primary) and NZ Herald each state the breach.

review.note: stronger/different than source: Seekom does not say it cannot confirm a link; it says messages appear to contain booking info from its platform but it cannot know for sure. Also council changed to campground.

evidence.quote: We identified unauthorised access to that platform on 20 November 2026.
